Every city has a second life that begins when most people stop looking. A baker unlocks a door before dawn. A streetlight blinks off above an empty intersection. Somewhere, a night bus sighs at the curb, carrying one passenger home and another toward work. These moments rarely become stories, yet they hold the day together.

I like to imagine attention as a form of hospitality. When I notice something carefully, I make room for it without demanding that it entertain or improve me. The cracked cup can remain cracked. The sparrow on the fence owes no symbolism. Even silence is allowed to be only silence, resting between one sound and the next.

This is harder than it sounds. My mind prefers bargains: beauty in exchange for praise, effort in exchange for certainty, kindness in exchange for being remembered. But the world keeps offering gifts with no invoice attached. Rain darkens the pavement. A stranger holds an elevator. Bread warms the air. None of it asks to be deserved.

Perhaps freedom begins here, in the small decision to receive a moment without immediately turning it into something else. Not every experience needs a lesson. Not every joy needs a witness. Sometimes it is enough to stand at the window, feel the cool glass beneath my fingers, and let the unfinished morning arrive. You do not have to understand it. You only have to leave a little space, and listen while the ordinary world continues. Softly, patiently, and entirely without asking permission.
